segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah, thanks for making time, Dana. I had us down to talk about the renewal for the analytics workspace and the 12 additional viewer seats for the finance team.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Yep, that's right. Current term runs through March 31, and we'd like the added seats live by February 12 if the numbers work.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Got it. You're at 48 seats today, 22 full users and 26 viewers. Adding 12 viewers brings the total to 60. On the annual plan, that puts the renewal at $54,600 before tax, including support.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Okay. Is that based on a 12-month renewal starting April 1, or are you prorating the new seats from February?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Good question. The 12 viewer seats would be prorated from February 12 through March 31, that's $1,080. Then the 60-seat renewal starts April 1 for the full year at $54,600.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: That lines up. Procurement will ask whether the payment terms stay net 30 and whether the data processing addendum is the same one we signed last year.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yes, net 30 stays the same. And the DPA is unchanged from the August version you already have on file. I'll include that reference in the order form so legal doesn't have to re-review the whole thing.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Perfect. One thing, our controller wants invoices split by department: 40 seats to corporate and 20 to finance. Can billing handle that?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yes. We'll set the invoice split at 67% corporate and 33% finance, with the two PO numbers you send over. If you can get those to me by Friday, the February 12 go-live is fine.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: I can do that. Send the order form today, and I'll route it for signature. Assuming no surprises, we should have it back by February 6.
